messages:
maria: Heads-up — during today's private-deploy drill we hit a scenario: a compromised tenant workload ended up with a mounted node-level service-account token and accessed the onprem keystore. Need immediate containment + a short-term rotation/runbook. :rotating_light:
cheng: ugh. do we have timeline + audit evidence? which token, pod, node?
maria: timeline in cluster-audit logs. root access was via svcacc:tenant-ingest, token mounted by a legacy sidecar. Node: node-az2-178. first access 11:07:23 UTC. attached sample log: ```audit.log: {"ts":"2026-03-03T11:07:23Z","verb":"token.exchange","user":"system:serviceaccount:tenant:tenant-ingest","node":"node-az2-178","resource":"keystore/decrypt","result":"ok"}```
priya: if token was node-mounted, short-term fix = revoke token, force pod eviction, rotate keystore envelope keys. but need to coordinate with customer KMS policy (HSM-backed) — can we rotate envelopes without downtime?
sam: steps I propose for immediate containment: 1) cordon node-az2-178, 2) evict tenant pods with grace 0, 3) revoke svcacc tokens for namespace tenant, 4) apply networkpolicy to isolate keystore service to only keystore-proxy in kube-system, 5) trigger keystore key wrapping key (KWK) rotation.
mike: +1. I can take node cordon/evict and svcacc rotation. priya — can you own KWK rotation with ops?
priya: I can. we need to confirm the keystore supports rolling rewrap: rewrap(key_id) -> new_envelope, update secrets provider, then signal runtime. If not, we may need short ephemeral outage window (2-3m) to do atomic swap.
cheng: audit query I'm running: ```kubectl --context=onprem-a audit-logs --since 30m | jq 'select(.resource=="keystore/decrypt")'``` will post findings. also check kubelet logs on node for file mount ops.
maria: posted the list of affected pods (short): tenant-ingest-7f6d, lt-sidecar-2, tenant-cache-0. Node logs show sidecar initiating curl to 10.0.2.12:8321
sam: network policy snippet to apply immediately (deny by default, allow only keystore-proxy): ```apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: keystore-isolate
  namespace: default
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: keystore
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  ingress:
  - from:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          kube-role: system
    - podSelector:
        matchLabels:
          app: keystore-proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8321```
priya: that looks good. also add egress block from tenant namespace to prevent lateral calls: ```NetworkPolicy allow-only-dns-and-ecr``` (short policy that only allows 53 and egress to KMS endpoints)
mike: doing cordon/evict now. will update when tenant pods evicted.
secops-bot: [alert] Keystore: unusual decrypt volume mount detected on node-az2-178 at 2026-03-03T11:07:23Z. Incident ticket created: INC-2026-314.
maria: action items — (1) cheng: collect full audit dump + kubelet mounts (due in 20m), (2) mike: cordon/evict + rotate svcacc tokens (now), (3) priya: plan+execute KWK rewrap (estimate 30m), (4) sam: push netpols & egress restrictions (now). i'll coordinate comms to customer security SLA.
cheng: audit dump posted to the incident channel and attached S3 link (internal). found three distinct tokens used between 11:07-11:09. also found kubelet K8s volume source: hostPath:/var/run/secrets/tenant/token.
sam: netpol applied to keystore namespace and egress restriction to tenant namespace. test: curl from tenant pod to 10.0.2.12:8321 -> connection refused.
mike: svcacc tokens rotated. evicted pods restarted on other nodes; verified auth can-i checks now fail on the old tokens: ```kubectl auth can-i decrypt --as=system:serviceaccount:tenant:tenant-ingest``` -> "no"
priya: starting KWK rewrap now. procedure: 1) call kms.rewrap(key_id) -> new_envelope, 2) push new envelope to keystore config, 3) rolling restart keystore replicas one at a time, 4) verify decrypt success using new envelope. Posting command sequence in incident doc.
maria: reminder: this highlights two gaps we should close postmortem: a) prohibit hostPath mounts of service account tokens in tenant namespaces (policy + OPA gate), b) keystore should enforce mutual TLS and client cert pinning to proxy, not rely on tokens alone.
cheng: agree. add automated audit alert for any hostPath mount of "/var/run/secrets" from workloads not in kube-system.
mike: logging note — ensure keystore access logs include envelope key id and origin node ip for forensic correlation. added to ticket INC-2026-314.
priya: KWK rewrap completed, rolling restarts done, verified decrypt with new envelope. no customer-visible failures.
sam: recommend immediate RBAC change: remove cluster-wide 'impersonate' scope from our tenant support role; restrict to namespaced ops where strictly required.
maria: good call. i'll open PR for RBAC tightening and OPA gate. assigning reviewers: @cheng, @sam.
secops-bot: [resolved] Keystore decrypt abnormal access — containment validated. Incident INC-2026-314 status: mitigated.
maria: postmortem to follow. thanks everyone for fast response. :trophy:
